properties.abstract: This single track is over 10 kilometres in length. Passing beneath the limestone rock faces of the Rätikon mountain range, it is considered a gem for cyclists in the Prättigau. The track has flowy and technical sections as well as breathtaking views. Following the Alpine trail to Schuders and traversing the wild Schrabachtobel ravine, the ride through the valley comes to an end in Schiers.
properties.description:
St. Antönien is a typical Walser village, nestled in a magnificent mountainous landscape. At first, the route leads uphill following in the original tracks of the legendary “Swiss Bike Masters” bike race. Via Aschüel on a partially surfaced little road, the trail climbs beneath the avalanche barriers of the Chüenihorn up to the Bärgli (2,135 metres above sea level). 

Then comes the single track with views that grow ever more spectacular as you cycle along – expect to be wowed when you reach Sulzfluh. Continue on to Carschinasee lake (where there is a barbecue area and a rowing boat) and through hilly terrain to the Carschinahütte SAC cabin (2,221 metres above sea level; not taking overnight stays in summer 2025 due to renovations, outdoor dining Monday to Friday, closed weekends). Once this first part of the route is behind you, it is a good time to take a break, as you’ve already covered 11 kilometres and around 900 metres of elevation.

Now for the real meat of the journey: a varied single track (S2) leads west along the Prättigau High Trail. Areas of scree alternate with areas of pasture and you will have to cycle around the odd boulder. Concentration is key, but you may want to stop and enjoy the views from time to time during the impressive passage beneath the limestone rock faces of the Drusenfluh massif. The single track follows this high trail for a glorious seven kilometres with relatively little altitude difference (400 metres downhill and 100 metres up). Around 500 metres after branching off to the Schweizertor pass, you will then tackle the steepest part of the descent. There are a couple of tricky stretches (S2+) to overcome on the last two kilometres of the single track before you reach the Alpine trail uphill from the Grüscher Älpli. 

Now the route follows the gravel road to Schuders. Exposed stretches call for careful cycling, as you will be sharing the road with oncoming traffic. In Schuders, take a sharp left onto the Sagenweg (Story Trail), which winds steeply downhill into the Schrabachtobel ravine. Note: if there is a sign reading “Tobelstrasse gesperrt” (Tobelstrasse road is closed), you will have to follow the surfaced road to Schiers.

Schrabach is one of the biggest torrents in Switzerland and is also known for the glimpses it provides of the folds of the Bündner schist. In parts, the forest road is only maintained as a gravel road. After the leisurely ride through the wild ravine, the tour ends in the valley village of Schiers.
properties.title: Rätikon Bike
